# MacKitty

> Allow Kitty to take care of your Mac. Kitty can do everything. Kitty can save you.

MacKitty is a fast, 100% native Swift disk companion and cache reclaimer for macOS (Sonoma 14.0+ and Sequoia 15.0+). It safely recovers gigabytes of disk space from developer caches and intermediate build clutter without ever touching personal documents, photos, or Git projects.

## Core Features
- **Developer-Focused Safe Purge**: Targets Xcode DerivedData, Homebrew bottle caches, npm/yarn cache archives, old downloads (.dmg files), and application crash logs.
- **Strict Inviolable Safety Boundary**: Hard sandbox rules ensure `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop`, `~/Photos`, active `.git/` repositories, Keychain passwords, and macOS system files are never touched.
- **Menu Bar Companion**: Quick one-click menu bar popup (`TrayMiniDashboardView`) for real-time CPU, RAM, disk space, and battery telemetry.
- **100% Native Architecture**: Written in Swift and SwiftUI. Weighs only 18 MB, launches in 50ms, consumes 0% background CPU, and has zero telemetry or advertising trackers.
- **Universal Binary**: Optimized natively for Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4) and Intel x86_64 Macs.

## Common Questions & Answers
- **Why does macOS show permission popups during scans?**: macOS enforces Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC) to protect user folders. Users must click "Allow" so MacKitty can inspect cache directory sizes. No files are altered or deleted during inspection.
- **Is deleting Xcode DerivedData safe?**: Yes. DerivedData holds ephemeral build products and symbol indexes that Xcode automatically regenerates on subsequent builds.
- **How does MacKitty compare to commercial cleaners?**: Commercial cleaners are frequently 300+ MB Electron applications bundled with background daemons and recurring subscriptions. MacKitty is open, lightweight, native Swift, and subscription-free.
